subject: SCIM & SSO artifact delivery plan for SIG audit
messages:
From: Bethany Cruz <bethany.cruz@medisync-health.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SCIM snapshot + SSO assertion samples for SIG

Hi Sean,

We're running through our SIG questionnaire for an upcoming audit and need a few artifacts to close the access control section. Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated delivery date? Our ask list below — short and specific so our auditors can accept straight into the portal: 

- SCIM user snapshot (tenant: medisync-prod) for 2025-06-01 -> 2025-07-01 (CSV with username, externalId, email, active flag, groups)
- Example SAML assertion for a typical end-user login (include NameID, subject/email, attribute statements) — sanitized is OK if you note what was removed
- RBAC mapping export (role -> permissions, example service account entries called out)
- Short narrative (1–2 paragraphs) describing SSO flow and how least-privilege is enforced (who can grant admin roles, review cadence)

We aim to upload everything to our audit portal by 2025-07-22. If you can provide a firm delivery date and preferred transfer method (SFTP / presigned S3 / shared Drive), that would help.

Attached: Medisync_SIG_checklist_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Bethany Cruz
Security Architect
Medisync Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Cruz <bethany.cruz@medisync-health.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SCIM snapshot + SSO assertion samples for SIG

Hi Bethany — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (security) and Marissa (CS) so we can scope and schedule. Quick answers up front: we can produce all of the items you listed. Proposed plan: 

1) SCIM snapshot: a CSV export scoped to "medisync-prod" for the 2025-06-01 -> 2025-07-01 window. We'll include username, externalId, email, active, and group membership. PII handling: we recommend delivering the CSV with emails present (auditors generally need them) but can redact on request; if you need redaction indicate whether you want hashed emails or truncated values.

2) SAML assertion example: we will provide a sanitized assertion text file showing NameID and attributes. We'll preserve attribute names and value formats but obfuscate the specific identifier values (can provide a mapping file under NDA if you need exact values).

3) RBAC export: CSV mapping role -> permissions and a separate file for service_account_roles.csv listing service accounts and their assigned roles.

4) Narrative: short 2-paragraph doc explaining our SSO flow (IdP->SP exchange, session handling, JIT provisioning via SCIM, and how elevated roles are granted and reviewed).

Delivery & transfer: we can stage artifacts in a short-lived presigned S3 folder (recommended) or SFTP/Drive if you prefer. Proposed delivery date: 2025-07-20. Can you confirm that date works for your upload deadline?

I'll attach a small evidence index (evidence-index.md) that we'll populate as files are produced. Laura — can you confirm the redaction default and whether we should include checksums for every file?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Bethany Cruz <bethany.cruz@medisync-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SCIM snapshot + SSO assertion samples for SIG

Thanks Sean. Confirming our defaults and adding a couple of internal notes for the delivery: 

- Redaction policy: auditors typically need email addresses present. We'll deliver the SCIM CSV with email values intact. For any user PII beyond email (SSNs, etc.) — which we do not store — we will not include.
- SAML assertion: we'll provide a single sanitized assertion (saml_assertion_sample.txt) that preserves attribute names and types. We'll include a short README that explains which fields were obfuscated and why.
- Checksums & transfer: we'll upload artifacts to a presigned S3 path and include SHA256 checksums for each file in the evidence-index.md. This avoids Drive/FTP permission issues and is auditable.
- RBAC export: role->permission mapping plus service_account_roles.csv. We will also include a short line-item mapping of policy names to the canonical permission set used by Redwood (helps auditors map semantics).

Internal ask to Marissa / Sean: please confirm whether you want us to include daily session logs or just the provisioning snapshot; Medisync's checklist asks for session traces in one field but that often isn't necessary for SIG unless the auditor specifically requests behavioral logs.

Deliverable ETA: we will target 2025-07-20 EOD PT for the initial bundle (files + evidence-index + readme). If Medisync needs earlier delivery for review, we can push to 07/18 for the core artifacts (SCIM + SAML sample).

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Security — Redwood Inference

From: Bethany Cruz <bethany.cruz@medisync-health.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SCIM snapshot + SSO assertion samples for SIG

Hi all — this looks great, thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications: 

- 2025-07-20 ETA is fine. We will accept presigned S3. Please send the link and checksums when ready.
- For SCIM, please include group membership lines — our auditors expect to see role-like groups mapped to RBAC entries.
- Session logs: not required now; we will only request them if the auditor flags an exception during intake.

Also looping in procurement: Charles Nguyen <charles.nguyen@procure.cloud> — Charles, please assist with any PO/DocuSign we need for evidence transfer if required.

If you can send the presigned S3 path + checksums by EOD 2025-07-20, that will let us close the access controls section.

Thanks again,
Bethany Cruz
Security Architect
Medisync Health
